summary.one_liner: Bloom is an AI personal tutor that builds a syllabus for any topic and teaches one adaptive lesson at a time, using a Claude Code skill (CLI) or a React/FastAPI web app.
summary.what_it_does: Bloom generates a structured syllabus for a topic, then delivers lessons one at a time. The reader annotates text and writes feedback, and the next lesson is adapted to those annotations and to answers to thought questions. The CLI mode is a dependency-free Claude Code skill (bloom-tutor) copied into a project's .claude/skills folder, with a separate set of learn-* skills (deep, crossover, occam, graph, prototype, feynman) for other learning angles. The web mode is a React + Vite frontend with a FastAPI + SQLite backend that works with any OpenAI-compatible LLM API. Web courses can start from a topic, an uploaded PDF/TXT/MD source, or a set of project files, and the app includes highlight Q&A, next-topic recommendations, and a learning calendar. The README says the CLI skill makes no network calls beyond the configured LLM endpoint.
use_cases: learn a new subject with an AI tutor
turn a textbook chapter or paper into guided lessons
study from my own PDF or markdown notes
self-paced course with quizzes and feedback
track mastery across a multi-lesson course
run a private AI study tool in the browser or terminal
how_to_run: mkdir -p .claude/skills && cp -R skills/bloom-tutor .claude/skills/ (CLI mode, then run claude)
cd backend && uv sync && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev
docker compose up -d (Docker option, after filling in .env)
notable: Two modes from the same flow: a Claude Code skill with no backend, and a full web app
Adaptive lessons that address gaps from the learner's annotations and feedback
Highlight-to-ask Q&A inside any lesson or source, with answers feeding the next lesson
Portable learn-* skills, each dependency-free, for different learning approaches
Works with any OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint
caveats: The web mode needs an OpenAI-compatible API key and a Python plus Node.js setup, or Docker
The CLI mode requires Claude Code
The README does not say how output quality varies across LLM providers or topics
